module_title: Factors of Industrial Location and Specific Clusters
introduction: Why is an industry established in one specific place and not another? At this level, we analyze the 'Factors of Industrial Location'. We will see how the nature of the raw material (like weight-losing properties) dictates the geography of Sugar, Jute, and Aluminum industries, and why Information Technology (IT) thrived in Bengaluru.

core_concepts.title: Weight-Losing Raw Materials
core_concepts.description: Some raw materials lose a massive amount of weight during the manufacturing process. For example, making sugar from sugarcane: 100 tonnes of sugarcane yields only about 10 tonnes of sugar. To save on exorbitant transportation costs and to prevent the sucrose content from drying up during transit, 'Sugar Mills' are always located directly adjacent to sugarcane fields, never near distant consumer markets.

core_concepts.title: Jute Industry and the Hooghly Basin
core_concepts.description: India is the largest producer of raw jute in the world. The vast majority of India's jute mills are located in 'West Bengal', clustered in a narrow belt along the banks of the Hooghly River. The reasons include: proximity to the jute-producing areas, abundant water for 'retting' (processing) the raw jute, cheap water transport, cheap labor from neighboring Bihar and UP, and the Kolkata port for export.

core_concepts.title: Aluminum Smelting
core_concepts.description: This is the second most important metallurgical industry in India. The process of extracting aluminum from alumina requires a 'massive and uninterrupted supply of electricity'. Therefore, aluminum smelting plants are always located directly next to large Power Plants or major dams (e.g., near the Hirakud dam in Odisha, or Hindalco in UP), rather than near the raw material.

core_concepts.title: Information Technology (IT) Industry
core_concepts.description: The electronic capital of India is 'Bengaluru', widely known as the 'Silicon Valley of India'. Unlike steel or sugar, the IT industry is NOT dependent on heavy raw materials. It developed here due to the availability of highly skilled human resources, a pleasant climate, excellent educational institutions, and highly favorable state government policies. Hyderabad and Pune are other major hubs.

important_entities.name: Southward Shift of the Sugar Industry
important_entities.description: In recent years, the sugar industry has shown a distinct tendency to shift and concentrate in the southern and western states, especially Maharashtra. The geographical reasons are: 1. The cane produced there has a 'higher sucrose content'. 2. The cooler climate ensures a 'longer crushing season'. 3. The cooperative societies are far more successful in these states compared to the north.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A highly conceptual trap: In the cotton textile industry, raw cotton does NOT lose weight during manufacturing (100 kg of cotton makes 100 kg of yarn). Thus, cotton mills can be located near the market. However, in the sugar industry, the raw material loses immense weight. Therefore, sugar mills are 'field-bound' and can only be located near the farms.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Water (Hooghly river), Agriculture (Bengal's raw jute), Labor (from Bihar/UP), Port (Kolkata). These four factors perfectly explain the concentration of the jute industry in the Hooghly basin.

exam_strategy_tips: If a question asks which industry's location is entirely dictated by the 'availability of cheap and regular electricity', choose 'Aluminum Smelting'.
In Assertion-Reasoning questions, perfectly align the concentration of jute mills in West Bengal with the geographical availability of water for retting and cheap labor.
